questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Salesforce's documented requirements for deploying Apex to production?
options: At least 75% org-wide code coverage
All tests complete successfully
All classes and triggers compile successfully
Every class must individually have 100% coverage
questions.explain: The requirement is 75% coverage computed org-wide, not 100% coverage on every individual class — plus every trigger needing some coverage, all tests passing, and successful compilation.

questions.q: A codebase sits at 85% org-wide coverage, but one previously-passing test now fails after a recent change. Can it deploy to production?
options: Yes, because coverage is well above 75%
No — all tests must complete successfully, which is a separate requirement from the coverage percentage
Yes, as long as the failing test isn't a trigger test
It depends on which Salesforce edition the org is on
questions.explain: Coverage and 'all tests passing' are two separate, simultaneous requirements — a single failing test blocks deployment regardless of how high the coverage percentage is.

questions.q: What does a validation-only deployment do differently from a real deployment?
options: It skips running tests entirely to save time
It performs every check a real deployment would (compile, test, coverage) without actually committing the changes to the target org
It only checks compilation, not test coverage
It automatically fixes failing tests
questions.explain: A validation-only deployment runs the full set of checks — compilation, tests, coverage — without committing any changes, letting a team catch problems before attempting the real deployment.

questions.q: A team runs only the tests for the specific classes they changed and sees them all pass locally. Why might a real deployment to production still get blocked?
options: Running specific tests always counts double toward coverage
The org-wide coverage average is computed across the entire org's Apex, so a shortfall elsewhere can still block the deployment even if the changed classes' own tests all passed
Specified-test deployments are never allowed in Salesforce
This scenario cannot happen — passing the tests you ran always guarantees deployment success
questions.explain: The 75% coverage requirement is computed org-wide, not just for the classes being deployed — a coverage shortfall in unrelated, untouched code can still block the deployment.

questions.q: What is the main risk of writing throwaway tests purely to push org-wide coverage over 75%, without real assertions?
options: Apex will refuse to compile such tests
It satisfies the deployment gate once but leaves the code no safer against future regressions, since nothing meaningful is actually being verified
It automatically triggers a security review
It permanently locks the org's deployment pipeline
questions.explain: Coverage without real assertions games the number rather than achieving its purpose — the deployment technically succeeds, but the underlying code remains just as unprotected against a future regression as before.
